claims.title: Exact one-way INDEX causal-cut lower bound
claims.scope: deterministic zero-error one-way answering of every coordinate of an m-bit record when the query is revealed after the message is fixed
assumptions: every coordinate remains an allowed future query
the decoder receives no record-dependent information beyond the declared message or resident state
nonclaims: if the query is known before communication, the m-bit conclusion does not apply
the result does not identify parent-universe hardware or prove simulation

claims.title: Uniform bounded-error causal-cut information lower bound
claims.scope: uniform independent m-bit records, a uniformly random post-message coordinate query, and average query error epsilon in [0,1/2]
assumptions: shared randomness is independent of the hidden record
the decoder answer for coordinate i is a function of its record-dependent message and shared randomness
nonclaims: the information lower bound is not asserted to equal exact finite communication complexity for every m and epsilon
mutual-information bits are not automatically physical storage or energy

claims.title: Weighted-query coordinatewise-Fano optimization
claims.scope: uniform independent source bits, a declared nonnegative query-weight vector summing to one, and weighted average error epsilon
assumptions: coordinatewise binary Fano bounds are used to upper-bound conditional entropy
only the weighted average error constraint is supplied
nonclaims: the KKT solution optimizes this information lower-bound relaxation rather than proving exact finite weighted INDEX complexity
zero-weight coordinates are outside the declared future query support

claims.title: Resident-memory and one-way communication cut tradeoff
claims.scope: one answering region with s record-dependent resident bits and c additional pre-query communication bits
assumptions: the resident state and communication together contain all record-dependent information available before the unresolved query
the bounded-error case uses the uniform source and query model
nonclaims: the division between memory and communication is architecture-dependent
shared randomness populated using the record must be counted as state or communication

claims.title: Isolated answer-region storage replication
claims.scope: r physically separate answer regions, each with its own finite local state, no later communication, and no record-dependent shared store
assumptions: each region must answer its own post-separation future query under the declared error model
local storage lengths are summed across regions
nonclaims: replicated copies do not contain r times as much unique global mutual information
the replication factor fails if all regions retain access to one shared record-dependent store

claims.title: Indexed parity reconciliation is one-way INDEX
claims.scope: one region holds remote record A, the answering region holds local record B, and query i asks for A_i xor B_i
assumptions: B_i is locally known when the parity answer is produced
the remote-record message is fixed before query i is revealed
nonclaims: the equivalence concerns the remote contribution and does not count storage of the local record B
does not imply every distributed physical comparison is an INDEX instance

claims.title: Prefix-storage random-access upper construction
claims.scope: uniform m-bit records and uniform coordinate queries when the first s record bits are stored exactly and every other coordinate is guessed zero
assumptions: unstored source bits are independent and uniform
the deterministic decoder guesses zero outside the stored prefix
nonclaims: the prefix protocol is an illustrative upper bound rather than an optimal random-access code
its gap from the Fano lower bound remains explicit
